questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.**

We __congratulated him at__ his new job. He was delighted.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**congratulated him on**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us understand the implication of the correct collocation:
 
• **Congratulated him on**: to **compliment someone and express approval or happiness** on a noteworthy or exceptional accomplishment.
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *He **congratulated me on** my wedding.*
 
• *I** congratulated him on** his promotion.*
 
 
 
 
 
• It is apparent from the above explanation that **"c**ongratulated him on" is an** appropriate collocation** instead of **"c**ongratulated him at".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: *We** ****congratulated him on__** his new job. He was delighted.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's know more about collocation:
 
• In the English language, **collocation is the regular pairing of two or more words with a frequency greater than chanc**e. It describes a natural **combination of words that are strongly related to one another.**
 
• **Adjective + adverb, noun + noun, verb + noun, **and so forth are forms of collocations.
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *surge of anger*
 
• *burst into tears*
 
• *a fastfood joint*

This mango is __bitterer.__

• The underlined part of the sentence, "**bitterer**," is incorrect because it uses the comparative form inappropriately.

questions.question:
**Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'.**

One must do __his work__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'one's work'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **"One must do one's work"** is correct because it uses the singular form "**one**" consistently throughout the sentence.
 
• In this case, "**one**" is used as **an indefinite pronoun**, referring to **an unspecified person **in a general sense. When using "**one**" as **a subject, **it's typical to maintain the consistency by using **"one's"** as **the possessive pronoun.**
 
• Here is the sentence breakdown: 
 
 
• **"One must"** is the subject followed by the verb **"must."** This structure is commonly used to indicate a general obligation or requirement.
 
• **"Do one's work"**: **"Do"** is the verb, and "one's work" is the object. "One's" is a possessive pronoun used to show that the work belongs to the indefinite person referenced as "one."
 
 
 
• This construction maintains consistency and clarity by using the same indefinite pronoun ("one") and its corresponding possessive form ("one's") within the sentence.

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *One must do** one's work. ***

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Abu said that __he saw the picture__.

options.text: he will have seen the picture
he would have seen the picture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **he had seen the picture**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is divided into two clauses.
 
• The conjunction (**that**) joins the parts of the sentence.
 
• Whenever two clauses are joined by a conjunction and one is written in the **simple past tense**, the other one must be written in the **past perfect tense**.
 
• The **past perfect** refers to a time earlier than before now. It is used to make it clear that one event happened before another in the past.
 
• The structure follows: **Subject + had + v3+ object.__**
 
• So, "**had seen**" should be used in the given sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

**Corrected sentence:** *Abu said that he had seen the picture.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The government is developing a new test __in the recruitment and training of teachers__ in the upcoming session.

options.text: in recruitment and training on teachers
of the recruitment and training of teachers
for the recruitment and training of teachers
for recruitment or training of teachers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. for the recruitment and training of teachers .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition **"for"** is the most appropriate choice when expressing the purpose or intention of an action, which is applicable in this context.
 
• The phrase **"for the recruitment and training of teachers"** clearly conveys the purpose of the test being developed by the government.
 
• Other prepositions like **"in"**, **"of"**, or **"on"** do not convey the intended meaning as accurately as "for."

Correct sentence: *The government is developing a new test for the recruitment and training of teachers in the upcoming session*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Prepositions:**
 
 
• **For:** Indicates purpose or intention. Example: This is a tool for cutting wood.
 
• **In:** Indicates inclusion or location. Example: She is in the room.
 
• **Of:** Indicates possession or relation. Example: The tail of the dog is wagging.
 
• **On:** Indicates position or surface. Example: The book is on the table.

Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Food prices in Switzerland are __as expensive to__ the rest of Western Europe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. more expensive than .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence compares food prices in Switzerland with the rest of Western Europe, which requires the use of the **comparative degree** of the adjective.
 
• The correct comparative form of "expensive" is **"more expensive than"**, as it is a multi-syllable adjective that forms its comparative with "more" instead of "-er".
 
• The phrase **"as expensive to"** is incorrect because "to" is not used for making comparisons; "than" is the correct preposition for comparison.
 
• Option 1 (**"the most expensive than"**) is incorrect because "the most expensive" is the superlative degree, which is used to compare one item with all others in a group, not just two entities.
 
• Option 4 is incomplete and does not form a proper comparative structure.

Correct sentence: *Food prices in Switzerland are **more expensive than** the rest of Western Europe.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:**

 
 
• Used to compare two entities.
 
• Formed by adding "-er" to short adjectives (e.g., taller, bigger) or using "more" with longer adjectives (e.g., more beautiful, more expensive).
 
 
 
• **Superlative Degree:**
 
 
• Used to compare one entity with a group.
 
• Formed by adding "-est" to short adjectives (e.g., tallest, biggest) or using "most" with longer adjectives (e.g., most beautiful, most expensive).

Avika understands French, __does she__?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'doesn't she'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect. **
 
• A positive statement is followed by a negative question tag.
 
 
• *Example: Mary can speak English, can't she?*
 
 
 
• A negative statement is followed by a positive question tag.
 
 
• *Example: They aren't funny, are they?*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the negative tag of **'does'** should be used. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.** 

 ​

**Correct sentence:__** *Avika understands French, **doesn't she?***

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Indeed, Jack is one of __the clever__ men I have ever met.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2 – "the cleverest"**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the phrase **"one of the"**, which must be followed by a **superlative degree** adjective to compare Jack with a group of people.
 
• Among the given options, **"the cleverest"** is the correct superlative form of “clever.”
 
• The use of **"most clever"** is also a superlative, but when a one-syllable adjective like "clever" has an "-est" form available, it is more natural and preferred in standard usage.
 
• Options like “clever” (positive degree) and “cleverer” (comparative degree) are not grammatically appropriate in this sentence structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2 – "the cleverest"**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Indeed, Jack is one of the **cleverest** men I have ever met."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Superlative adjectives are used with “one of the…” to show that someone/something belongs to a group characterized by the highest degree of a quality.
 
• Examples: “She is one of the **best** dancers,” “This is one of the **most interesting** books I’ve read.”

The assignment __was so difficult__ for Mohit to do all by himself.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The correct answer is option 1 i.e. 'was too difficult'.**
 
• **Rule**__: The adverb '**too**' should be followed by "**adjective + to infinitive(to + V1)**". 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the adjective (difficult) is followed by 'to + V1' i.e. 'to + do'.
 
• So, according to the rule, the adverb **'so' should be replaced by 'too'**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is 'The assignment **was too difficult** for Mohit to do all by himself.'
